SUNRIDGE GOLDENS – HEALTH GUARANTEE POLICY
Version: 2.1   Effective: January 1, 2024
[Supersedes v2.0 dated June 1, 2022]

1. COVERAGE PERIOD: Breeder guarantees puppies against hereditary health conditions for TWO (2) years from date of birth.
2. ELIGIBLE CONDITIONS: OFA-recognized hereditary conditions including but not limited to: hip dysplasia (grade moderate or severe), elbow dysplasia, progressive retinal atrophy, subvalvular aortic stenosis.
3. BUYER OBLIGATIONS: Buyer must (a) maintain annual vet examinations, (b) provide vet records on request, (c) notify breeder in writing within 30 days of diagnosis.
4. REMEDY: At breeder's discretion: replacement puppy from next available litter OR 50% refund of purchase price.
5. EXCLUSIONS: Conditions caused by injury, neglect, or improper diet are not covered.

documents.content:
GREENFIELD FARMERS MARKET – TRADER MEETING MINUTES
Date: 2 April 2024, 6:30 pm, Greenfield Community Hall
Attendees: R. Hooper (chair), Claire Sutton, Dave Marsh, Yuki Tanaka, Priya Nair, ~14 others

1. Fee increase notice. R. Hooper advised stall fees will increase from $42 to $48 per week from the start of the 2024 season (May). Reason: increased council permit costs.
2. Electricity. New hookup points installed at 6 power-enabled bays. Fee $6/day. Traders to apply in writing.
3. Parking. Loading bay access extended to 7:00 am Saturdays.
4. Any other business. Claire Sutton asked about honey-labelling requirements – R. Hooper to follow up with council.

Next meeting: TBC. Minutes recorded by Yuki Tanaka.

Date: 11 Mar 2025
Subject: Group travel insurance – school trip Paris June 2025

Hi,

I'm organising a school trip to Paris (18–21 June 2025) for 44 students and 4 staff (48 people total). Could you send me a quote for group travel insurance? We'll need cover for medical, cancellation, and lost luggage.

The trip cost per head is £310. We are a secondary school in England.

Marie Hendricks
St Bridget's School

documents.title: Insurance quote reply from SchoolTravelCover
documents.content:
From: quotes@schooltravelcover.com
To: m.hendricks@stbridgets.sch.uk
Date: 13 Mar 2025
Subject: RE: Group travel insurance – school trip Paris June 2025

Dear Ms Hendricks,

Thank you for your enquiry. For a group of 48 travelling to France for 4 days, our Group Explorer policy covers:
- Medical & repatriation up to £5m per person
- Cancellation up to £500 per person
- Lost/delayed luggage up to £250 per person

Premium: £12.50 per person = £600 total for 48 people.

Policy can be added to your booking up to 14 days before departure. Quote valid 30 days.

Kind regards,
SchoolTravelCover Team

Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs
Rural Payments Agency
Date: 14 November 2023

Dear Mr Whitaker,

Basic Payment Scheme – Single Farm Payment 2023
SBI Number: 107443829

We are pleased to confirm your BPS payment for the 2023 scheme year has been calculated as follows:

Entitlements claimed: 48.62 hectares
Payment rate: £128.40 per hectare
Gross payment: £6,243.71
Cross-compliance deduction (2%): £124.87
NET PAYMENT: £6,118.84

Payment will be credited to your nominated bank account on or around 1 December 2023.

If you disagree with this decision you have 60 days to request a review.

Yours sincerely,
J. Patel, RPA Case Officer

Handwritten note at bottom: "Arrived 20 Nov – less than last yr (was £6,400 approx)"

documents.title: Sunridge Pediatrics Allergy Policy Extract
documents.content:
SUNRIDGE PEDIATRICS – ALLERGY MANAGEMENT POLICY (excerpt)
Effective: January 1, 2024

Section 4.2 – Action Plan Renewal
All anaphylaxis action plans must be renewed annually and submitted to the child's school and any overnight program at least 14 days prior to the start date.

Section 4.3 – Epinephrine Prescriptions
Epinephrine auto-injectors should be replaced when expired or after any use. Prescriptions are written for a 365-day supply with up to 3 refills. Parents are advised to check expiration dates at the start of each school year and each camp session.

Section 4.4 – Benadryl (Diphenhydramine) Dosing
For children 6–11 years: 12.5 mg per dose (5 mL of 12.5mg/5mL liquid), up to 3 doses per day. Dosing is weight-dependent; confirm with physician at each annual visit.

documents.title: Carer Support Meeting Minutes – May 2024
documents.content:
Harrogate Carer Support Network
Monthly Meeting – 9 May 2024, 10:30am
Venue: Harrogate Central Library, Meeting Room 2
Chair: Pat Drummond
Attendees: Sharon Mellor, Gail Firth, Tom Rees, Pat Drummond

Minutes:
1. Apologies received from Brenda Cole.
2. Sharon updated the group on Derek's recent hospital admission (3–7 April 2024). Discharge went smoothly.
3. Sharon mentioned her April respite booking had gone well and she was planning an August booking.
4. Pat reminded members that the Carer's Emergency Card scheme is available through North Yorkshire Council – members should carry one.
5. Gail raised concerns about delayed benefit payments; Pat to follow up with DWP liaison.
6. Next meeting: 13 June 2024, same venue, 10:30am.

Actions: Pat – DWP liaison contact. Sharon – look into emergency card.

documents.title: Text Message Thread Summary (Sharon & Jenny Marsh)
documents.content:
Text message summary – saved by Sharon Mellor, 25 July 2024

Jenny (Sunnyside) → Sharon, 23 Jul 10:14am:
"Hi Sharon, just a reminder the August balance of £840 is due by 27 July. Give us a call if there are any problems!"

Sharon → Jenny, 23 Jul 11:02am:
"Hi Jenny, I've done a bank transfer this morning for the full £840. Should clear tomorrow. Thanks, Sharon"

Jenny → Sharon, 24 Jul 2:37pm:
"Great news – payment received, all confirmed for August. Derek's room will be Room 14 again. See you on the 10th! 😊"

Sharon → Jenny, 24 Jul 3:05pm:
"Brilliant thank you. Will there be the same activities programme as April? Derek really enjoyed the chair yoga."

Jenny → Sharon, 24 Jul 3:22pm:
"Yes, chair yoga is on Tuesday and Thursday mornings. We've also added a new reminiscence session on Wednesdays."

[Note added by Sharon: "must remind Derek to pack his slippers this time!"]

documents.title: Choir Committee Meeting Minutes – 15 January 2025
documents.content:
HARTWELL HARMONY CHOIR – Committee Meeting
Date: 15 January 2025   Venue: Okafor home (informal)
Present: Adaeze Okafor (Treasurer), Bev Marsh (Chair), Tom Ricci (Secretary)

1. Venue hire: Adaeze confirmed deposit to Hartwell Village Hall. NOTE – letter had wrong session count; corrected version expected. Target: 7 sessions at £45.

2. Dues: Agreed to hold full membership at £85 for 2025 (up from £75 last year). Concession raised to £50. Associates £25.

3. Grant: Application MAC-2025-0394 submitted Dec 2024, awaiting outcome. Fingers crossed!

NSW DEPARTMENT OF PRIMARY INDUSTRIES
BIOSECURITY INSPECTION REPORT

Inspection Date: 18 April 2024
Inspector: Jake Morello, Senior Biosecurity Officer (DPI Dubbo)
Property: 'Wirragulla' Station, Narromine NSW 2821
PIC: NH220417
Farmer: Dale Hutchinson

Get Robbo to quote — ring him Mon morning.
Don't leave it til the last minute like the water trough thing last time.

documents.content:
GREENFIELD SUMMER FESTIVAL
Volunteer Policy – Section 4: Shift Requirements (approved 1 March 2025)

4.1  All volunteers must attend a mandatory briefing no later than 48 hours before their first shift.
4.2  Volunteers working shifts of 6 hours or longer are entitled to one 30-minute meal break and two 15-minute rest breaks.
4.3  Volunteers under 18 years of age may not be assigned to Gate or Parking duties without a parent/guardian consent form on file.
4.4  A volunteer coordinator must be reachable by radio at all times during event hours.
4.5  No-show without 24 hours notice will be recorded and may affect future volunteering eligibility.

documents.title: Email thread – query about osmosis treatment cost
documents.content:
From: me@example.com
To: bookings@northernsurveysltd.co.uk
Date: 04 April 2024  18:42
Subject: Quick question – osmosis treatment

Hi Colin,

Following up on the March survey – the port-quarter blistering, do you think I need to treat it this season or is monitoring sufficient for now?

Also roughly what would epoxy barrier coat treatment run to for a 26-footer?

Thanks

---
From: colin.marsh@northernsurveysltd.co.uk
Date: 05 April 2024  08:55

Hi,

Honestly at this stage monitoring is fine – it's very minor. I wouldn't spend money on full treatment yet. Reassess next haulout.

For a full epoxy barrier on a Centaur you'd be looking at a boatyard quote, probably £600–£900 depending on yard, not something we price for. Worth getting two or three quotes if you do decide to go ahead.

Colin

Called SolarBright 6 May – spoke to Priya.
She confirmed scaffold comes down approx 5 days after install.
Asked about adding extra panel – she said 7th panel would add ~£350 + VAT to quote but would need new structural check (£150 extra). Decided NOT to go ahead with 7th panel – sticking with 6.

Also – Priya said MCS cert usually comes 2–3 weeks after install. Need MCS cert to register for SEG export payments with Octopus.

documents.title: Greenfield FM Stallholders Meeting – Minutes, 5 March 2024
documents.content:
Greenfield Farmers Market – Stallholders Meeting
Date: 5 March 2024, 6:30 pm, Greenfield Community Hall
Attendees: Sarah Holt (chair), Pete Mallory, Diane Ferris, Raj Patel, others (approx 12 total)

documents.content:

Grantor: Kellner Civic Trust

documents.title: Pledge Reminder Letter – Kellner Civic Trust
documents.content:
August 8, 2024

Dear Ms. Okafor,

This letter serves as a reminder that the second disbursement of your Kellner Civic Trust grant (KCT-2024) in the amount of $11,250 is scheduled for release on October 1, 2024, contingent on receipt and approval of your Q2 interim report.

Your Q2 report submitted July 12, 2024 has been reviewed and approved. The disbursement of $11,250 will proceed as scheduled.

Please confirm receipt by emailing grants@kellnertrust.org.

Sincerely,
Robert Fitch
Grants Manager, Kellner Civic Trust

documents.title: Informal Notes – Vega Foundation LOI Prep (Oct 2024)
documents.content:

- Deadline: Oct 31, 2024 – DO NOT MISS
- Asking amount: $75,000 (board approved Sept 18)
- Focus: senior services expansion, specifically meal delivery + case mgmt

- Contact there: Miriam Castillo, program officer

- Anita to draft, Priya to review by Oct 28

documents.title: Lakeview Elementary – Allergy & Medication Policy Extract (2024–25)
documents.content:
LAKEVIEW ELEMENTARY SCHOOL
Allergy & Medication Administration Policy
Effective: September 2024

Section 3.2 – Epinephrine Auto-Injectors
All students with a documented anaphylactic allergy must have two (2) epinephrine auto-injectors on file with the school nurse. Devices must not be expired. Parents are responsible for replacing expired devices within 14 days of expiration notice.

Section 3.4 – Antihistamines
Antihistamines (e.g., diphenhydramine, cetirizine) may be kept by the nurse with a valid physician's note. A prescription label on the original container is sufficient documentation.

Section 3.7 – Allergy Action Plans
An updated Allergy Action Plan must be submitted at the start of each school year and whenever allergens or medications change. Plans must be signed by a licensed physician.

Section 4.1 – Nut-Free Classrooms
All Grade 3–5 classrooms are designated nut-free zones. Students may not bring peanut or tree nut products.

documents.title: Lakeview Elementary – Allergy & Medication Policy Extract (2024–25)
documents.content:
LAKEVIEW ELEMENTARY SCHOOL
Allergy & Medication Administration Policy
Effective: September 2024

Section 3.2 – Epinephrine Auto-Injectors
All students with a documented anaphylactic allergy must have two (2) epinephrine auto-injectors on file with the school nurse. Devices must not be expired. Parents are responsible for replacing expired devices within 14 days of expiration notice.

Section 3.4 – Antihistamines
Antihistamines (e.g., diphenhydramine, cetirizine) may be kept by the nurse with a valid physician's note. A prescription label on the original container is sufficient documentation.

Section 3.7 – Allergy Action Plans
An updated Allergy Action Plan must be submitted at the start of each school year and whenever allergens or medications change. Plans must be signed by a licensed physician.

Section 4.1 – Nut-Free Classrooms
All Grade 3–5 classrooms are designated nut-free zones. Students may not bring peanut or tree nut products.

Sheffield S1 2SH

documents.title: Household Admin Meeting Notes – February 2024
documents.content:

Agenda: car stuff

2. Insurance coming up in June – need to compare quotes before auto-renewal kicks in. Sarah said to try comparethemarket. Last year we paid £689, hoping for less this time. NOTE: check no-claims is recorded correctly (should be 4 years).

3. Service was expensive – £222 all in. James moaning about it. Sarah pointed out the air filter probably needed doing.

4. MOT: reminder set on phone for September 2024.

5. ACTION: James to call Admiral before 23 June re black box discount.

Meeting ended ~8pm.

Hollow Tree Records, 18 Denmark St, London WC2H
5 March 2025

Dear Maya,

Re: INV-2025-005 – Sync Licence Fee (TV Advertisement)

Thank you for your invoice of £750.00 for the sync licence granted for the Blythe & Co cosmetics advertisement (UK broadcast, Jan–Mar 2025).

We are withholding payment pending clarification of the territorial scope agreed in your original licence memo dated 9 December 2024. Our records indicate the licence was limited to online/digital platforms only and did not include broadcast television rights.

We would appreciate your response within 14 days of this letter.

Yours sincerely,
Jodie Marsh
Royalties & Licensing Manager, Hollow Tree Records

5 March 2025

Dear Maya,

Thank you for your invoice of £750.00 for the sync licence granted for the Blythe & Co cosmetics advertisement (UK broadcast, Jan–Mar 2025).

Yours sincerely,
Jodie Marsh

NOT COVERED: Injuries, illnesses due to buyer negligence, Parvo or Distemper if vaccination schedule not maintained.

Policy supersedes all prior versions.

8 August 2024

Bristol City Council Parking Services

Re: PCN BCC-2024-099341 – informal appeal

Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing to challenge the above PCN issued on 7 August 2024 for vehicle KL19 VFP at Queen Square.

I was loading/unloading items for a disability support visit (my mother, who is a blue badge holder). I was present at the vehicle throughout. I believe the contravention was incorrectly recorded.

James Whitmore

Dear Mr Whitmore,

Thank you for your informal appeal against PCN BCC-2024-099341.

After reviewing the evidence provided, we are pleased to advise that your appeal has been ACCEPTED and the Penalty Charge Notice has been cancelled.

No further action is required and no payment is due.

If you have already made payment, please contact us to arrange a refund.

Kind regards,
Bristol City Council Parking Services

documents.title: Training plan overview – Spring block (handwritten scan)
documents.content:
Spring block – wk 1 starts Mon 4 March

Wk 1-3: base miles, aim ~200km/wk, keep HR zone 2
Wk 4: recovery – drop to 100km, no intervals
Wk 5-8: build phase – add 2x Tue threshold sessions (20 min @ FTP)
Wk 9: second recovery week
Wk 10-12: race-specific – long Sunday ride min 5hrs, include Haytor climb x2
Wk 13: taper – reduce vol by 40%, keep one short interval session
Event week: easy spin Mon, REST Tue-Sat, race Sunday 23 June

Note: FTP test scheduled Sat 2 March – need result before block starts!
Current FTP estimate: 238w (from last Nov test)
Target FTP by wk 5: 255w

Exe Valley Cycling Club – Committee Meeting
Date: Thursday 8 February 2024, 19:30
Venue: The Thatched Inn back room
Present: Sarah Okafor (chair), James Holloway, Pete Drummond, Anita Rees

Apologies: none

1. Club sportive entries – Pete confirmed 4 members entering Dartmoor Classic. James noted he has upgraded to Gran Fondo.

2. Club kit order – Anita to coordinate bulk order via Sigma Sports. Deadline for individual orders: 20 February. James has already placed individual order.

Carer's Allowance Unit, Wolverhampton WV98 2BW

Dear Ms Sandra Hollis,

Your Carer's Allowance has been awarded at the rate of £81.90 per week, payable every four weeks in arrears.

Yours sincerely,
Carer's Allowance Team

Yours sincerely,
Carer's Allowance Team

documents.title: Stall Holder Meeting Minutes – 18 February 2024
documents.content:
MILLBROOK FARMERS MARKET – STALL HOLDERS MEETING
Date: 18 February 2024, 6:30 pm, Village Hall Annexe
Chaired by: Patricia Holt  |  Notes: R. Gibbs

Attendees: Donna Marsh (Sweet Hollow Apiary), Pete Okafor (Okafor Veg), Sandra Li (Li's Preserves), Tom Whitmore (Whitmore Cheese)

Item 3 – Fees for 2024 season: Patricia confirmed fees would stay at £22.50 per date until April, after which a review would take place. Donna asked whether table hire would still be available. Patricia confirmed yes at £3.00 per table.

Item 5 – Summer market: Dates agreed as 4 May, 1 June, 6 July, 3 August 2024.

AOB: Donna noted she plans to bring new wildflower honey range in June.

documents.title: Text message thread summary – Donna & Tom re May invoice
documents.content:
Summary of WhatsApp exchange between Donna Marsh and Tom Whitmore, saved 9 May 2024.

Donna (8 May, 10:14): "Tom did you get a new invoice from the market? Mine's gone up to £110 total. They've charged £24 per stall now."

Tom (8 May, 10:31): "Yeah same here. Patricia sent that letter in April – think it was always going to go up, just annoying. I'm paying mine today."

Donna (8 May, 11:02): "Ok fair enough. Still gonna query the parking permit – I didn't ask for one. £4 seems small but it adds up over the season."

Tom (8 May, 11:15): "Agree, worth raising. She's usually reasonable."

documents.title: Donna's handwritten note – honey stock for May market
documents.content:

- Clear blossom: 24 jars (250g) @ £4.50 each
- Set blossom: 12 jars (250g) @ £4.50 each
- Wildflower: 10 jars (340g) @ £6.00 each
- Creamed honey: 6 pots (250g) @ £5.00 each

Remember: take card reader + spare batteries
Float: £40 in change

documents.content:

Thank you for invoice MFM-2024-052 dated 7 May 2024. I have a query regarding the parking permit line (£4.00). I do not recall requesting a parking permit for the May date and would be grateful if you could clarify whether this is now a mandatory charge or an error.

I am otherwise happy to pay the remainder of the invoice (£106.00) promptly and will settle the outstanding amount once this is resolved.

Yours sincerely,
Donna Marsh
Sweet Hollow Apiary
07712 334 509

Sara: Best I can do is £1,750 for the quartz – saves you £90. Total would then be £11,620.

Next step: sign and return acceptance form to Hartley by 28 March 2025 (quote expires 13 April 2025).

County Buildings, Market Street, Dunmore
4 February 2024

Dear Mr Hadley,

I am pleased to confirm your Basic Payment Scheme (BPS) entitlement for the 2024 scheme year.

Your eligible area has been assessed at 47.3 hectares. Your payment rate is £214.00 per hectare. Your total indicative payment is therefore £10,122.20.

P. Walsh

Region 4 Office
22 March 2024

Dear Mr Hadley,

Notice of Scheduled Farm Inspection

An inspection of Hadley Farm will take place on Thursday 18 April 2024 between 09:00 and 13:00. The inspection will cover:

If you need to rearrange please call 01472 556 200 at least 5 working days before the appointment.

Yours faithfully,
Animal Health & Welfare Inspectorate, Region 4

documents.title: Meeting Minutes – Hadley Farm / Riverside Mill feed review, Jan 2024
documents.content:
MEETING MINUTES
Date: 16 January 2024
Attendees: Tom Hadley (farmer), Janet Cross (Riverside Mill rep)
Venue: Hadley Farm kitchen

1. Review of 2023 feed performance – Layer pellet FCR improved to 2.1. Janet confirmed new formula rolled out Q4 2023.
2. Pricing 2024 – Janet confirmed layer pellets hold at £8.50/bag for Q1. Price review scheduled for Q2 (April).
3. Next order window – Tom to place March order by 5 March. Delivery lead time 5–7 working days.
4. Sunflower cake – Tom asked to trial 5 bags of sunflower cake 25kg alongside standard order.
5. Any other business – Tom raised issue of last November delivery arriving short by 3 bags layer pellets. Janet to credit on next invoice. Credit of £25.50 agreed.

Minutes recorded by: Janet Cross

documents.title: WhatsApp summary – Sarah re: consumables budget (16 Jan 2024)
documents.content:

Priya: ugh ok. how long does that normally take

documents.title: Supervisory Meeting Minutes – 15 Jan 2024
documents.content:
SUPERVISORY MEETING MINUTES
Date: 15 January 2024, 14:00
Present: Prof. O. Tarkington (supervisor), Dr R. Mehta (co-supervisor), Priya Nair (student)

1. Progress update: Priya presented preliminary confocal data from 8 Jan session. Good signal-to-noise; repeat run suggested for sample batch B.
2. Next booking: Priya to book confocal suite for w/c 29 January 2024 (full day if possible).
3. Stipend query: Priya flagged she hadn't received December uplift yet. Prof T. to chase Graduate Office. Revised monthly amount should be £1,421.

Next meeting: 12 February 2024, 14:00
Minutes recorded by: R. Mehta

documents.title: WhatsApp summary – Sarah re: consumables budget (16 Jan 2024)
documents.content:
Text summary saved from WhatsApp chat with Sarah (lab manager) – 16 Jan 2024 ~10:30am

Priya: hey Sarah quick q – does PO HW-PO-3392 cover the immunostaining kit on invoice BSL-7741?
Sarah: hi! so that PO is only for general consumables up to £150 total. the immunostaining kit is a specialist item, it needs its own PO
Sarah: you need to fill in form RB-12 and get Tarkington to sign it
Priya: ugh ok. how long does that normally take
Sarah: usually 5 working days once signed
Priya: ok thanks will do it today
Sarah: also the £179.30 subtotal doesn't include VAT obviously – finance will want the full £215.16 on the claim form
Priya: got it cheers!

Dear Mr Ashworth,

Section 3 – Minimum Health Requirements for Breeding Stock:
3.1 All breeding dogs must have current OFA hip evaluation (Good or Excellent) and CAER eye exam within 12 months prior to breeding.

4.1 All puppies receive wellness exam, microchip, and dewormer at 6 weeks.
4.2 First DHPP vaccine administered at 8 weeks.
4.3 All puppies microchipped before leaving the property.

COASTAL MARINE SURVEYS
Report Ref: CMS-2024-0188
Date of Survey: 26 March 2024
Vessel: Saltwind  LOA: 32ft  Type: Bermuda sloop
Owner: D. Calloway  Berth: 14B, Brightwater Harbour

SUMMARY
Hull condition: Satisfactory. Minor osmotic blistering noted on starboard quarter – recommend epoxy treatment within 12 months.
Keel bolts: 3 of 8 show surface corrosion – monitor, re-examine within 6 months.
Rigging: Standing rigging serviceable. Forestay swage terminal showing early fatigue – REPLACE BEFORE NEXT PASSAGE.
Engine: Not within scope of this survey.

OVERALL CONDITION: SATISFACTORY WITH NOTED DEFECTS
Surveyor: Pete Okafor MRINA

Netherton NE4 7PP
18 March 2024

Dear Mr Okafor,

Yours sincerely,
Sal Merton
The Brickyard Café
